overall: The Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law. The January 28 minutes were sufficiently accurate despite omitting that the motion was seconded; the AG recommended, but did not order, correcting the typo.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the January 28 minutes are inaccurate because they state a motion was made to approve legal counsel when, she claimed, no such motion was made.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the minutes accurately summarize the discussion on this topic and record the outcome of the vote that was taken.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the January 28 minutes fail to note that the motion to approve legal counsel was seconded.
allegations.key_passage: while it is a best practice for public bodies to note in their minutes that motions were made and seconded prior to a vote, listing these procedural steps is not a requirement of the Open Meeting Law.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
